semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {مِنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب}: «مِنْ» may be for clarification, so it is attached to an omitted element, i.e., "I mean from the People of the Book". The second: it is a ḥāl from «الذين كفروا».
His saying: {مِن دِيَارِهِمْ}: attached to «أَخْرَجَ»; its meaning is the beginning of the limit. Annexing the homes to them is sound because they built them.
His saying: {لأَوَّلِ الحشر}: this lām is attached to «أَخْرَجَ» and is the lām of timing, as in His saying {لِدُلُوكِ الشمس} [al-Isrāʾ: 78], i.e., at the first gathering. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the lām in His saying the Exalted {ياليتني قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي} [al-Fajr: 24] and in your saying 'I came for such-and-such a time'." I say: the discussion of this lām will come in al-Fajr, God willing.
His saying: {مَّانِعَتُهُمْ حُصُونُهُم}: two views. One: «حصونُهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «مانِعَتُهم» a fronted khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «أنهم». It is not to be said: why not say «مانِعَتُهم» is the mubtadaʾ because it is definite, and «حصونُهم» its khabar? There is no need for fronting or postponing, because the intention is to report about the fortresses, and because the annexation is not a true one (ghayr maḥḍa), so it is indefinite. The second: «مانِعَتُهم» is the khabar of «أنهم» and «حصونُهم» is the agent through it, like "inna Zaydan qāʾimun abūhu" and "inna ʿAmran qāʾimatun jāriyatuhu". The Shaykh preferred it, because in the like of "qāʾimun Zaydun", whether it be a fronted khabar and postponed mubtadaʾ, there is disagreement, and the Kufans forbid it; so the place of agreement is preferable.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what difference is there between your saying 'and they thought that their fortresses would protect them', or 'protectors of them', and the arrangement in which it came? I say: in fronting the khabar before the mubtadaʾ there is an indication of the extreme of their confidence in the fortresses' strength and in their protecting them, and in making their pronoun the noun of «أنَّ» and predicating the clause of it there is an indication of their belief about themselves that they were in might and defence such that they cared nothing for anyone who might confront them; and that is not in your saying 'their fortresses protect them'." End of quotation. What he mentioned works only on the first i'rab, and it has already been mentioned that it is the weaker. Here "thinking" is made to operate on the doubled «أنَّ», though the rule is that nothing operates on it or on its lightened form except a verb of knowledge and certainty; so [thinking] is treated like certainty because of its strength and because it stands in the position of knowledge.
His saying: {يُخْرِبُونَ}: it may be resumptive, to report it, and it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قلوبِهم», though not likely. Abū ʿAmr read «يُخَرِّبون» doubled and the rest lightened; they have one meaning, because Abū ʿAmr made kharraba transitive by doubling and they by the hamza. From Abū ʿAmr it is reported that he distinguished them with another meaning, saying: "kharraba with doubling: he demolished and spoiled; and akhraba with hamza: he left the place in ruins and went away from it." Al-Hudhalī preferred Abū ʿAmr's reading for the sake of intensification. «يُخْرِبون» may also be an explication of the terror, so it too has no position.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {الجلاء}: the majority [read it] with the lengthened form, which is expulsion: ajlaytu al-qawma ijlāʾan, and jalā he went into exile, jalāʾan. Al-Māwardī said: "Al-jalāʾ is more specific than leaving, because it is said only of a group, while expulsion applies to a group or one." Another said: the difference between them is that jalāʾ is with family and children, unlike expulsion, which does not require that.
Al-Ḥasan and ʿAlī, sons of Ṣāliḥ, read «الجَلا» with an alif only. Ṭalḥa [read it] with hamza without alif, like «al-naba'». Ṭalḥa read «ومَنْ يُشاقِقْ» with unassimilated doubling, as is agreed upon in al-Anfāl.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {مَا قَطَعْتُمْ}: «ما» is conditional, in the position of the accusative through «قَطَعْتم», and «مِن لينةٍ» is a clarification of it. «فبإِذنِ اللهِ» is the apodosis of the condition. An omission is necessary, i.e., "its cutting is by Allah's permission", so «بإذنِ الله» is the khabar of that mubtadaʾ. There is much disagreement about the līna. It is said: it is the palm tree in general, and he recited:
4244 - As if my saddle-frame upon her were a bird's nest ... on a long-stemmed palm whose sides sway
and another said:
4245 - Wings spread, settled above a līna ... the dew of its night glistening on its feathers
It is also said: it is the palm tree that is not an ʿajwa. It is also said: that which is neither ʿajwa nor barniyya. It is also said: the noble palm. It is also said: a palm whose dates are a "colour" (lawn), a kind of date; Sufyān said: it is intensely yellow, translucent to the stone. It is also said: it is the ʿajwa. It is also said: it is the saplings (fusilān), and he recited:
4246 - They planted a līna by a flowing stream ... then the palms were enclosed with thickets
and another said:
4247 - The loved ones have shunned me when they sang ... of parting from the loved ones, from atop a līna
It is also said: it is the tree's branches, for their softness.
There are two views on the ʿayn of «لِينة». One: it is a wāw, because it is from lawn (colour), and it was turned into yāʾ because of its quiescence and the kasra before it, like dīma and qīma. The second: it is a yāʾ, because it is from līn (softness). The plural of līna is līn, because it is of the type of collective noun like tamra and tamr. It has also been broken as «līyān», which is irregular, because breaking what is distinguished by the feminine tāʾ is irregular, like ruṭaba, ruṭab and arṭāb. He recited:
4248 - And a neck like the crushing of the līyān ... which the misguided one set afire with flames
The pronoun in «تَرَكْتموها» returns to the sense of «ما». ʿAbd Allāh, al-Aʿmash and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «قُوَّماً» on the pattern of ḍurrab, plural of qāʾim, observing the sense of «ما», which is plural. «قائماً» has also been read, singular masculine. «أُصُلِها» has also been read without wāw. There are two views: one, that it is the plural of aṣl, like rahn and ruhun. The second, that he dropped the wāw as heavy.
His saying: {وَلِيُخْزِيَ}: the lām is attached to an omitted element, i.e., "and He permitted cutting it so that He may disgrace", or "so that He may gladden the believers and strengthen them, and so that He may disgrace".

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {فَمَآ أَوْجَفْتُمْ}: the fāʾ is the apodosis of the condition, or redundant, on the basis that it is a relative noun containing the sense of a condition. «ما» is negative. Al-ījāf is making a camel go at a quick pace; one says wajafa the camel, yajifu, wajfan, wajīfan and wajafānan. I made it do so: awjaftuhu ījāfan. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
4249 - A swift one, whom weariness from his trotting had folded up
and Nuṣayb said:
4250 - How many a riding party whose trotting I have crossed ... to you, and but for you the party would not have trotted
His saying: {مِنْ خَيْلٍ}: «مِنْ» is redundant, i.e., "horses". Al-rikāb are the camels.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {مَّآ أَفَآءَ الله}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He did not insert a conjunction before this clause because it is an explanation of the first, so it is not foreign to it."
His saying: {يَكُونَ دُولَةً}: Hishām read «تكون» with the tāʾ and, [with it,] «دُوْلةٌ» nominative only; the rest [read] with the yāʾ and put «دُوْلَةً» in the accusative. As for the nominative, it is on the basis that it is the complete «كان». The masculine and feminine are clear since the feminine is figurative. As for the accusative, it is on the basis that it is the incomplete kāna; its noun is a pronoun returning to the fayʾ, and the masculine is necessary because of the masculine nominative; and «دُولة» is its khabar. It is also said that it returns to «ما», taking its wording into account. The majority read «دُوْلة» with ḍamma on the dāl; ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and al-Sulamī [read it] with fatḥa. It is said: they are equivalent, being what turns (yadūlu) for a person, i.e., revolves, of effort, hardship and victory. The experts among the Basrans, and al-Kisāʾī, said: al-dawla with fatḥa is from al-mulk with ḍamma on the mīm, and with ḍamma from al-milk with kasra; or with ḍamma in wealth and with fatḥa in victory. The reading transmitted from ʿAlī and al-Sulamī refutes this, since victory is certainly not intended here. «كيلا» is a reason for His saying «فللَّهِ وللرسول», i.e., its settling for such-and-such is for this reason.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لِلْفُقَرَآءِ}: three views. One: it is a badal from «لذي القُرْبى»; Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī said it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is said that it is a badal from «لذي القُربى» and what follows it." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "A badal from His saying «ولذي القُربى» and what is conjoined to it. What prevented substituting from «لله وللرسول» and what is conjoined to them, although the meaning is 'to the Messenger of Allah', is that Allah the Mighty and Majestic excluded His Messenger from the poor in His saying {وَيَنصُرُونَ الله وَرَسُولَهُ}, and that He the Exalted exalts His Messenger above being named poor, and that substituting according to the apparent wording departs from what is obligatory in glorifying Allah the Mighty and Majestic." He means: if it were said that it is a badal from «لله» and what follows it, what he mentioned would follow: that the badal, according to the apparent wording, would be from the Majestic Name, so one would say that «للفقراء» is a badal from «لله» and from «رسوله», which is ugly in wording, even if the meaning is contrary to this apparent sense, as he said: its meaning is "to the Messenger of Allah", and Allah the Mighty and Majestic is mentioned only for magnification, otherwise Allah the Exalted is free of need of the fayʾ and other things. He made it a badal from «لذي القُرْبى» only because he is a Ḥanafī, and the Ḥanafīs make poverty a condition for giving the relatives share from the fayʾ.
The second: it is a clarification of His saying {والمساكين وابن السبيل}, and the genitive lām was repeated, since the first was genitive by the lām, to make clear that the badal is from it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it, and it is a very unsettled expression. The third: «للفقراء» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e., "but the fayʾ is for the poor". It is also said: its implied form is "but it is for the poor". It is also said: its implied form is "wonder at the poor".
His saying: {يَبْتَغُونَ}: it may be a ḥāl. There are two views on its owner: one, «للفقراء»; the second, the wāw of «أُخْرِجوا». Makkī said both.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {والذين تَبَوَّءُوا}: two views are possible. One: it is conjoined to «الفقراء», so it is genitive, and is a conjunction of single words, with «يُحبُّون» a ḥāl. The second: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «يُحِبُّون», and then it is a conjunction of clauses.
His saying: {والإيمان}: several views. One: «تَبَوَّؤوا» is made to contain the sense of "adhered to", so conjoining «الإيمان» to it is sound, since faith cannot be "settled in". The second: it is accusative through an implied verb, i.e., "and they held as belief", or "and became accustomed to", or "and loved". Third: figurative usage is allowed with «الإيمان», making it, because of its mixing with them and their steadfastness in it, like a place surrounding them, as though they had alighted in it; on this he combined the literal and the figurative in one word, on which there is a well-known disagreement. Fourth: the original is "the abode of the hijra and the abode of faith", so the definite article in «الدار» took the place of the muḍāf ilayhi, and he omitted the muḍāf from "the abode of faith" and put the muḍāf ilayhi in its place. Fifth: that he named Medina so because it is the abode of the hijra and the place of the appearance of faith through faith. Al-Zamakhsharī stated these two views, and in it there is only the standing of «al-» in place of the muḍāf ilayhi, which is a point for consideration; what is known is the disagreement over whether «al-» stands in place of the pronoun that is the muḍāf ilayhi. The Kufans allow it, as in His saying the Exalted {فَإِنَّ الجنة هِيَ المأوى} [al-Nāziʿāt: 39], i.e., "its abode"; the Basrans forbid it and say that the pronoun is omitted, i.e., "the abode for him"; this has already been set out. As for its being a substitute for the muḍāf ilayhi, we know of no disagreement about it.
Sixth: it is accusative as an object of accompaniment (mafʿūl maʿahu), i.e., "together with faith"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it, and he said: "By this conjunction the meaning of His saying «مِن قبلهم» is sound, so consider it." I say: they made it a condition on the mafʿūl maʿahu that it may be conjoined to what precedes it, so that they made His saying {فأجمعوا أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمْ} of the type of implied verb, because one does not say "ajmaʿtu shurakāʾī", only "jamaʿtu"; this has already been discussed fully, praise be to Allah.
His saying: {حَاجَةً مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ}: two views. One: need here is in its normal sense of need, except that it stands in the position of what is needed; the meaning: they do not find any desire for what is needed from what the Emigrants were given of the fayʾ and other things, and what is needed is called a "need"; you say "take from him your need", and "he gave him from his wealth his need". Al-Zamakhsharī said so. On this the first pronoun is for those who came after the Emigrants, and the one in «أُوتوا» is for the Emigrants. The second: need here is from envy, as some said, the two pronouns being as before. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "a touch of need", i.e., the muḍāf was omitted because it is known; on this the two pronouns are for those who settled in the abode and in faith.
His saying: {وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ}: the wāw of ḥāl; its discussion has preceded.
Al-khaṣāṣa is need. Its origin is from khaṣāṣ al-bayt, which are its gaps, and the condition of the poor man is permeated by deficiency, so that was borrowed for it.
His saying: {وَمَن يُوقَ}: the majority [read it] with quiescent wāw and lightened qāf, from wiqāya. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Abū Ḥaywa [read it] with fatḥa on the wāw and doubled qāf. The majority [read] «شُحَّ» with ḍamma on the shīn; Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ibn ʿUmar with kasra.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {والذين جَآءُوا}: it admits the two views given above for «الذين» before it. If it is conjoined to the Emigrants, then «يقولون» is a ḥāl like «يُحبُّون», or resumptive; and if it is a mubtadaʾ, then «يقولون» is its khabar.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {لإِخْوَانِهِمُ}: the lām here is only for conveying, unlike His saying {وَقَالَ الذين كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ}, which admits that and admits cause. And His saying {وَلاَ نُطِيعُ فيكُمْ}, i.e., regarding fighting you, or regarding forsaking you.
And His saying {وَإِن قُوتِلْتُمْ لَنَنصُرَنَّكُمْ}: the implied oath is answered, because before «إنْ» there is a preparatory lām (lām muwaṭṭiʾa) which was omitted since its place is known, for it is most often brought. Like it is His saying: {وَإِن لَّمْ يَنتَهُواْ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ} [al-Māʾida: 73], which has already been discussed.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {لَئِنْ أُخْرِجُواْ لاَ يَخْرُجُونَ}: to the end: the oath is answered because it came first, and therefore the verbs are nominative and not jussive, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted since the answer to the oath indicates it; therefore the verb of the condition is in the past. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "His saying «لا يَنْصُرُوْنَهم»: since the condition is in the past, jussive was left off the answer." End of quotation. This is a mistake, because «لا يَنْصُرونهم» is not an apodosis of the condition; rather it is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted as its explanation preceded. It is as though he imagined that it is of the type of the saying:
4251 - And if a friend comes to him on a day of asking ... he says: my wealth is not absent, nor forbidden
Ibn ʿAṭiyya preceded Abū al-Baqāʾ in something suggesting this, but he stated explicitly that it is the answer to the oath, and said: "The verbs came non-jussive in «لا يَخْرجون» and «لا يَنْصُرون» because they return to the ruling of the oath, not to the ruling of the condition. In this there is something to consider." His saying "in this there is something to consider" suggests that it came contrary to what analogy requires, but that is not so; rather it came according to what analogy requires. There are two views on these pronouns. One: all of them are for the hypocrites. The second: they differ, some for these and some for those.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {لأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ رَهْبَةً}: «رهبةً» is a maṣdar from the passive «رُهِبَ», so the dread occurs in the hypocrites, not in those addressed, as though it were said: "you are more dreaded (marhūbiyya) in their breasts than Allah", so those addressed are feared. This is like the saying of Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr, may Allah be pleased with him, in praise of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
4252 - He is more fearsome to me when I speak to him ... while it is said: you are imprisoned and slain
than a lion in the thick of the land, whose lair ... in the belly of ʿAththar is a thicket beyond a thicket
And «رُهْبةً» is a tamyīz (specification).

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {جَمِيعاً}: a ḥāl, and {إِلاَّ فِي قُرًى} is attached to «يُقاتِلونكم».
And His saying: {جُدُرٍ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «جدار» in the singular. There are several views on it. One: he meant by it the wall, and the single wall covers all the fighters and shelters them. The second: it is a singular in the sense of a plural, as the context indicates. The third: each group of them is behind a wall, not that all of them are behind one wall. The rest read «جُدُر» with two ḍammas, considering that each group is behind a wall, so it was made plural for that. Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Ibn Wathāb and al-Aʿmash, and it is reported from Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim, [read it] with ḍamma and sukūn, a lightening of the first. Ibn Kathīr also read, in the transmission of Hārūn from him, and it is the reading of many of the Meccans, «جَدْرٍ» with fatḥa and sukūn; it is said that this is a dialect form of «al-jidār». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its meaning is the foundation of a building, like the wall and the like." He said: "It may be from jadr al-nakhīl, i.e., or from behind their palm groves." «جَدَر» with two fatḥas was also read, which al-Zamakhsharī related, and it too is a dialect form of «al-jidār».
His saying: {بَيْنَهُمْ}: attached to «شديد», and «جميعاً» is a second object, i.e., "gathered together", and «قلوبُهم شَتَّى» is a circumstantial clause, or resumptive, to report that. The majority read «شتى» without tanwīn because its alif is the alif of feminization. Among their sayings: "shattā taʾūbu al-ḥalaba", i.e., scattered. Another said:
4253 - To Allah I complain of a strife that has split the staff ... today it is scattered, yesterday it was united
Mubashshir ibn ʿUbayd read «شتىً» with tanwīn, as if he made it the alif of ilḥāq (extension).
[Translator's note: the source prints «وراية» for «رواية» (transmission) in "in the transmission of Hārūn"; translated as "transmission".]

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {كَمَثَلِ الذين}: the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e., "their likeness is the likeness of these". There are two views on «قريباً». One: it is accusative through the likening mentioned earlier, i.e., they are likened to them in a near time that will occur and not be delayed; then He clarified that with His saying: {ذَاقُواْ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِمْ}. The second: it is accusative through «ذاقوا», i.e., they tasted it in a near time that will occur and not be delayed. Its accusative on both views is as an adverb of time. And His saying: {كَمَثَلِ الشيطان} [al-Ḥashr: 16] is like a clarification of His saying {كَمَثَلِ الذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ}.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {فَكَانَ عَاقِبَتَهُمَآ}: the majority [read] «عاقَبَتَهُما» in the accusative, making it the khabar, and the noun is «أنَّ» and what is within its scope, because the noun is more definite than «عاقبتَهُما». The explanation of this was given in Āl ʿImrān and al-Anʿām. Al-Ḥasan, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and Ibn Arqam read it nominative, making it the noun, and «أنَّ» and what is within its scope the khabar, like the reading of {ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ} [al-Anʿām: 23].
His saying: {خَالِدَينَ}: the majority [read] it accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition phrase, because it occurs as the khabar. ʿAbd Allāh, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Aʿmash and Ibn Abī ʿAbla [read it] nominative as the khabar, with the adverbial disregarded (mulghā), being attached to the khabar; on this it is a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) of the particle, and the pronoun of what it indicates is repeated with it, like His saying: {فَفِي الجنة خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا} [Hūd: 108]. This is according to Sībawayh's view, for he permits disregarding the adverbial even if it is emphasized, while the Kufans forbid it, so this is an argument against them. They might answer: we do not concede that the adverbial in this reading is disregarded; rather we make it the khabar of «أنَّ» and «خالدان» a second khabar; this is capable of bearing what they say, but the apparent sense is otherwise.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {وَلْتَنظُرْ}: the majority [read] with quiescent lām of command. Abū Ḥaywa and Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith [read] it with kasra, in the original form. Al-Ḥasan [read] it with kasra and put the verb in the accusative, making it the lām of purpose (lām kay), and the thing for which it is the reason is implied, i.e., "let a soul look, [for] He has warned you and informed you". The indefiniteness of "soul" and "tomorrow": Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As for the indefiniteness of the soul, it is for the individuality of the souls that look at what they have sent forward for the Hereafter, as though it were said: let one single soul look. As for the indefiniteness of tomorrow, it is for magnifying it and leaving its matter vague, as though it were said: for a tomorrow whose true nature is not known, because of its greatness."
And His saying: {واتقوا الله}: emphasis. It is also said: it was repeated because the objects of the two fearings differ: the object of the first is fulfilling obligations, because it is joined to action, and of the second, leaving sins, because it is joined to threat and warning. Al-Zamakhsharī stated its meaning.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ}: the majority [read it] in the second person. Abū Ḥaywa [read it] in the third person, as a shift of address (iltifāt).

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {أَصْحَابُ الجنة هُمُ الفآئزون}: like an explanation of the negation of their equality. «هم» may be a separator (faṣl) and it may be a mubtadaʾ; on the first the report is by a single word, on the second by a clause.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {خَاشِعاً}: a ḥāl, because the seeing is visual. Ṭalḥa read «مُصَّدِّعاً», assimilating the tāʾ into the ṣād.
Abū Dharr and Abū al-Sammāl [read] «القَدُّوس» with fatḥa on the qāf. The majority read «المُؤْمِنُ» with kasra on the mīm, an active participle from āmana meaning "gave security". Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, and it is said Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, [read it] with fatḥa. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the sense of 'the one believed in', with omission of the preposition, as you say of Moses' people in His saying {واختار موسى قَوْمَهُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 155], 'the chosen ones'." Abū Ḥātim said: "That is not permitted, i.e., this reading, because if it were so it would be 'al-mu'man bihi' and he would be using the preposition; but 'al-mu'man' absolutely, without the preposition, would be one who was fearful and was given security." So he has refuted what al-Zamakhsharī said.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {الجبار}: those who say that forms of intensiveness may come from verbs beyond the triliteral cite it as evidence, for it is from ajbarahu ʿalā kadhā, i.e., he compelled him. Al-Farrāʾ said: "I have not heard faʿʿāl from afʿala except in jabbār and darrāk from adraka." End of quotation. Against him was added: asʾara, so he is saʾʾār. It is also said that it is from al-jabr, which is mending. It is also said: from their saying "a jabbāra palm tree", when the pickers cannot reach it. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4254 - Towering jabbār palms, thick of branch ... and they carried a cluster of red unripe dates

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {المصور}: the majority [read] with kasra on the wāw and nominative on the rāʾ: either as an adjective or as a khabar. The Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Ḥasan, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa read it with fatḥa on the wāw and accusative on the rāʾ. Its analysis: it is accusative through «الباري», and the "shaped one" (al-muṣawwar) is the human being: either Adam, or he and his children. On this reading it is forbidden to pause at «المصوَّر»; rather it is obligatory to continue so that the accusative shows in the rāʾ, otherwise something impermissible may be imagined from it in pausing. It is also transmitted from the Commander of the Faithful with fatḥa on the wāw and genitive on the rāʾ. It is like the first in meaning, except that he annexed the active participle to what it governs for lightness, like "al-ḍāribu al-rajuli". Pausing at «المصوَّر» in this reading is also forbidden; some have pointed that out. Makkī said: "Its accusative is permitted in speech, but the wāw must have fatḥa, and you put it in the accusative through «الباري», i.e., He is Allah, the Creator of the shaped one, meaning Adam, peace be upon him, and his children." End of quotation. I say: it has been read so, as preceded, and it is as though he did not come across it. He also said: "Its accusative is not permitted with kasra on the wāw, though it is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him." He means that when the wāw has kasra it is one of Allah the Exalted's attributes, and then its accusative is not straight in his view, because its accusative would be through the active participle before it. His saying "it is reported", i.e., kasra on the wāw and accusative on the rāʾ. If this is sound from the Commander of the Faithful, it is analyzed as being of the "cutting off" type (qaṭʿ), as though it were said: "I praise the Shaper", like their saying "al-ḥamdu lillāhi ahla al-ḥamd" with «ahla» accusative, and the reading of the one who read {للَّهِ رَبَّ العالمين} [al-Fātiḥa: 1] with «rabba» accusative. Makkī said: "al-muṣawwir is mufaʿʿil from ṣawwara yuṣawwiru, and it is not good for it to be from ṣāra yaṣīru, because it would follow that it be said 'al-muṣayyir' with yāʾ." The like of this is among the obvious, and the meaning does not accept it either.
